definition: The smallest piece of an element that can still be recognised as that element; splitting it further (into sub-atomic particles) needs nuclear processes, not chemistry.
msAccepts: smallest piece of an element still recognisable as that element

definition: Two or more atoms chemically bonded (by covalent bonds); the atoms may be of the same element (H2) or different elements (H2O).
msAccepts: two or more atoms chemically bonded/joined together
may be same or different elements
msAvoids: any group of atoms near each other

definition: The chemical bond that joins atoms into molecules, shown as a line between atoms in the book's diagrams; detailed treatment comes in later chapters.
msAccepts: bond between atoms in a molecule

definition: A particle smaller than an atom; the three of record are the proton, neutron and electron.
The central part of the atom containing the protons and neutrons; tiny compared with the atom but holding virtually all its mass.
msAccepts: centre of the atom containing protons and neutrons
msAvoids: the orbiting part of the atom

definition: Sub-atomic particle in the nucleus with relative mass 1 and relative charge +1; its number is the atomic number.
Sub-atomic particle in the nucleus with relative mass 1 and relative charge 0; its count varies between isotopes.
Sub-atomic particle outside the nucleus with relative mass 1/1836 and relative charge -1; its number equals the proton number in a neutral atom.
msAccepts: found outside the nucleus/around the nucleus
equal in number to the protons

definition: The number of protons in the nucleus of an atom; it defines the element and every atom of the same element shares it.
The total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus of an atom.
msAvoids: the bigger number on the Periodic Table (that can be the Ar)

definition: Atoms of the same element with the same atomic number but different mass numbers - same protons, different numbers of neutrons; chemically identical.
msAccepts: same atomic number, different mass numbers

definition: The average mass of an atom of an element, taking into account the amount of each isotope in a naturally occurring sample; a weighted average, usually not a whole number.
msAccepts: average mass of an atom of the element
takes into account the amount of each isotope
msAvoids: the mass of the heaviest isotope

definition: The amount (percentage) of each isotope present in a naturally occurring sample of an element.
msAccepts: percentage/amount of each isotope in a natural sample

definition: An average in which each value is multiplied by its weight before averaging; Ar weights isotope masses by their abundances.
msAccepts: average where values count according to their weight
multiply by weight, add, divide by total weight
msAvoids: a simple mean of equal parts

definition: The chart of all the elements, arranged in order of increasing atomic number; each cell carries the atomic number plus a mass number or relative atomic mass.
msAccepts: elements arranged in order of increasing atomic number
smaller number in the cell is the atomic number
msAvoids: arranged by atomic mass (that is not the ordering of record)

definition: What an atom becomes when it gains or loses electrons, so its particle counts stop matching; the book develops ions fully in Chapter 7.
msAccepts: formed when an atom loses or gains electrons
msAvoids: an atom that changed its proton number
